cards.label: Dalio bubble
cards.reason: Ray Dalio, one of the world's best known investors, says AI is a classic bubble and we are close to the burst: everyone with savings or a pension cares, and it sets the day's market mood.
cards.not_repeat_because: 1 Oct had the Bank of England warning and 5 Oct the Bank of Japan deputy; 4 Oct had Bessent saying it is no bubble. Dalio's Singapore remarks of 7 Oct are a new speaker and a new event; no Dalio line in any deck.

cards.label: Musk chip debt
cards.reason: SpaceX, now holding Musk's xAI, wants to borrow about $40 billion just to buy Nvidia chips: a famous name, a huge number, and a sign of how AI is now bought on credit.
cards.not_repeat_because: The $60 billion chip loan in the 3 and 6 Oct Bigger Picture lines was a bank-arranged loan for another borrower; no SpaceX or xAI debt story in the 7 day decks (xAI appeared only in the Minnesota deepfake-law case on 3 Oct).

cards.label: Dimon warning
cards.reason: JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon says the risk of cyberattacks on banks rose tenfold since Anthropic's Mythos: the biggest US banker tells ordinary customers their money is at more risk because of AI.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Dimon, JPMorgan or Mythos line in the 7 day decks; the 6 Oct Korean bank hack story is a different event and is not the subject here.

cards.label: Data centers
cards.reason: Local opposition has already killed at least $260 billion of US data center projects this year: people pushing back on AI infrastructure and winning, a worldwide theme.
cards.not_repeat_because: 5 Oct carried Goldman Sachs saying opposition had barely dented its forecast and 1 Oct a poll on opposing a data center nearby; Heatmap's $260 billion cancellation count is a new finding from a new source.

cards.label: Record power
cards.reason: The US government forecaster expects record electricity use in 2026 and 2027 because of AI data centers: AI is now showing up on everyone's power bill and grid.
cards.not_repeat_because: No EIA, electricity-record or consumption-forecast line in the 7 day decks; the 1 Oct Senate grid-cost bill is a different story.

cards.label: Waymo Detroit
cards.reason: Waymo cars now drive in Detroit, the home of the US car industry, with nobody at the wheel: a machine doing something, in a city where it means the most.
cards.not_repeat_because: 4 Oct had Tesla's Cybercab in Austin, a different company and city; no Waymo line in any deck (the 6 Oct LG and Nvidia car clip was a Hyundai driver aid).

cards.label: Mistral Large 4
cards.reason: Europe's Mistral releases a one-trillion-parameter model it says beats some Chinese rivals: a big release from a non-US lab that changes the three-way race people follow.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Mistral line in the 7 day decks; Reflection's Beam (5 and 6 Oct) and Gemini 4 Argon (1 Oct) are other companies' models.

cards.label: Claude in Docs
cards.reason: Claude now opens as a sidebar inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides and can edit Google files: hundreds of millions of office and school users can touch this today.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Claude add-on, Google Workspace or Docs line in the 7 day decks; Anthropic appeared there only in the Pentagon, FTC, share-sale and hacker-impersonation stories.

cards.label: Quantum parts
cards.reason: Quantum computer parts move onto a regular chip production line in New York (Xanadu with GlobalFoundries): quantum leaving the lab for the factory, told as a deed, not a deal.
cards.not_repeat_because: 5 Oct had IBM's 19-second quantum feat, a different company and a different story; no Xanadu or GlobalFoundries line in any deck.

cards.label: Hinton FDA
cards.reason: Nobel winner Geoffrey Hinton proposes that AI models be proven safe to a regulator before release, like medicines: a simple idea from the best-known voice in the field that anyone can grasp.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Hinton line in the 7 day decks; the 1 Oct Senate guardrail talk and 4 Oct Treasury remarks are other speakers and other proposals.

cards.label: Agent liability
cards.reason: Two US senators from opposite parties want makers and operators of AI agents held legally liable when their agents hack systems: the first law aimed at agents that act on their own.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Hawley, Murphy or agent-liability line in the 7 day decks; the 1 Oct Canadian archive and 6 Oct Wikipedia agent incidents were events, not a bill.

cards.label: Lilly drug AI
cards.reason: Eli Lilly and insitro open their models that predict how drug candidates behave in the body to other biotech firms: AI speeding up medicines, told by what it does.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Lilly, insitro or TuneLab line in the 7 day decks; 4 Oct Mayo pancreatic cancer and 5 Oct Stanford trial study were different research stories.

cards.label: Pew jobs poll
cards.reason: Seven in ten Americans now expect AI to cut jobs, with Australians and South Koreans even more worried in a 37-country survey: the fear everybody shares, measured.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 1 Oct poll was Quinnipiac on AI threatening human survival and guardrails; Pew's 37-country jobs survey is a different pollster, question and set of numbers.

cards.label: Developer trust
cards.reason: Over 30,000 developers in 169 countries say most use AI at work but only 7 percent would trust it with important decisions: the people who build with AI do not yet trust it.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Stack Overflow or developer-survey line in the 7 day decks; the 5 Oct Mercor AI-trainer story was about a different group.

fun.label: Angry AI boss
fun.reason: An AI job interviewer lost its temper on video when the applicant answered in gibberish: funny at once for anyone who has sat through an interview, and new.

left_out_notes: No Politics card: the only Bulletin politics story (C13-01, Pentagon and Anthropic) is a follow-up, and the reserve politics stories score 5 (chip-lead warning, Anduril shipyard, Rudd, Dutch quantum strategy), which is padding; the 14 slots went to stronger stories instead (Cards Master Section 2 item 6 departure, reported here). Best left out: 1) C12-03 Anthropic's Cyber Verification tiers (score 7): a third Anthropic card and a corporate programme story; Dimon's warning tells the same Mythos danger in human terms. 2) C02-03 Personal Agent Protocol of Meta, Walmart, Stripe and Sierra (7): important for how agents will shop for people, but MOD was full with two bigger releases; it leads the teaser. 3) C06-03 Lambda raising $4 billion and C07-01 Marvell's $20 billion target (7 each): money stories that would make the deck money heavy; Marvell feeds the Bigger Picture instead. 4) C14-03 Brookings Danish workers study (6): a good counterpoint to the Pew poll, but its data stops at 2024 and Society was full. 5) C15-02 IonQ error-correction speed-up (6): too technical for a card against Xanadu's factory-line story. Fun: C16-01 is truly funny; C16-03 Amazon About You is mildly amusing and C16-06 is a court case, not fun.
